# ⚡ Utility Vehicle Fleet Maintenance Tracker

![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-support%20services-blue)
![ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_ADK-v2.0-orange)
![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-Gemini_2.5_Pro-green)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of utility vehicle fleet maintenance tracker is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Utility Vehicle Fleet Maintenance Tracker Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank utility vehicle fleet maintenance tracker events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_support_services.utility_vehicle_fleet_maintenance_tracker_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "Which heavy-duty bucket trucks and boom lift vehicles have overdue dielectric boom testing or hydraulic fluid maintenance?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Fleet Telemetry and Maintenance Compliance records identify multiple heavy-duty bucket trucks and boom lift vehicles operating with overdue dielectric boom insulation certifications (per OSHA 1910.269/ANSI A92.2) and critical hydraulic fluid servicing intervals. Uncertified dielectric insulation presents an immediate personnel safety hazard during live-line work, while degraded hydraulic fluids risk catastrophic boom control failures. Immediate fleet grounding and work-order prioritization are required to clear regulatory non-compliance and maintain operational safety.**

---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Overdue Dielectric Testing (Fleet Count)** | 4 Units | 0 Units (100% On-Time) | +100.0% | **Critical** |
| **Overdue Hydraulic Fluid Service (Fleet Count)** | 4 Units | 0 Units (100% On-Time) | +100.0% | **Critical** |
| **Average Asset Health Index (AHI) - Overdue Units** | 61.4 / 100 | ≥ 85.0 / 100 | -27.8% | **Critical** |
| **Max Days Overdue (Dielectric Test)** | 45 Days | 0 Days | +100.0% | **Critical** |
| **Max Days Overdue (Hydraulic Service)** | 62 Days | 0 Days | +100.0% | **Critical** |

#### Overdue Vehicle Breakdown & Maintenance Schedule Status

| Vehicle ID | Unit Type | Make / Model | Grid Zone | Last Dielectric Test | Dielectric Status | Hydraulic Service Status | AHI Score |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BT-4012** | Heavy-Duty Bucket Truck | International 7400 / Altec TA60 | Zone-North | 13.5 mos ago | **Overdue (+45 Days)** | **Overdue (+15 Days)** | 54.2 (Critical) |
| **BT-4088** | Heavy-Duty Bucket Truck | Freightliner M2 / Terex Optima 55 | Zone-East | 12.6 mos ago | **Overdue (+18 Days)** | **Overdue (+28 Days)** | 62.0 (Warning) |
| **BT-4105** | Heavy-Duty Bucket Truck | Ford F-750 / Altec AA55E | Zone-West | 13.1 mos ago | **Overdue (+32 Days)** | Current (Due in 45 Days) | 68.5 (Warning) |
| **BL-2204** | Boom Lift Vehicle | Kenworth T370 / Bronto Skylift | Zone-Metro | Current (Due in 90 Days) | Current | **Overdue (+62 Days)** | 58.7 (Critical) |
| **BL-2219** | Boom Lift Vehicle | Freightliner M2 / Altec AT40 | Zone-South | 12.4 mos ago | **Overdue (+12 Days)** | **Overdue (+41 Days)** | 63.8 (Warning) |

---

---

### Actionable Recommendations
- **Immediate Lockout/Tagout (LOTO)**: Enforce dispatch lockout on units `BT-4012`, `BT-4088`, `BT-4105`, `BL-2204`, and `BL-2219` to prevent field deployment on energized high-voltage line work until certification is restored.
- **Expedite High-Voltage Dielectric Testing**: Schedule certified mobile laboratory dielectric testing for bucket trucks `BT-4012`, `BT-4105`, `BT-4088`, and `BL-2219` to comply with ANSI/SIA A92.2 annual dielectric requirements.
- **Hydraulic System Fluid Sampling & Flush**: Execute full hydraulic fluid drain, filter replacement, and particulate/moisture analysis for units `BL-2204`, `BL-2219`, `BT-4088`, and `BT-4012`.
- **Fleet Relief Reassignment**: Coordinate with Dispatch Operations to reassign compliant reserve utility bucket trucks to high-priority feeders across `Zone-North` and `Zone-Metro`.

---

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis
**User:** "Track fleet fuel consumption, engine idle hours, and scheduled preventive maintenance intervals across 450 service vehicles."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Fleet telemetry analysis across all 450 utility service vehicles indicates an aggregate fleet fuel efficiency of 11.8 MPG against a baseline of 13.2 MPG (-10.6%), driven primarily by elevated engine idle time averaging 35.4% of total runtime. A total of 26 vehicles (5.8%) currently exceed scheduled Preventive Maintenance (PM) thresholds, with Heavy Bucket Trucks and Digger Derricks representing the highest mechanical risk profile. Implementing automated idle-shutdown policies and batching overdue PM work orders will recover an estimated 8,400 gallons of fuel monthly and mitigate premature engine wear.**

---

### Actionable Recommendations

- **Prioritize Overdue PM Scheduling**: Immediately route the 20 heavy-duty assets (12 Bucket Trucks, 8 Digger Derricks) exceeding engine-hour PM thresholds to regional fleet maintenance bays to prevent PTO hydraulic and valvetrain degradation.
- **Enforce Engine Idle-Reduction Protocol**: Deploy automated auxiliary battery power units (e-PTO / ePTO hybrid systems) for aerial boom operation on heavy bucket trucks to eliminate continuous diesel engine idling during stationary line work.
- **Implement Tiered Telematics Geofence Alerts**: Configure telematics alerts to notify regional operations supervisors when vehicle idling exceeds 15 continuous minutes outside active emergency/storm response modes.
- **Standardize Engine Hour Maintenance Scheduling**: Transition heavy-duty aerial units from odometer-based PM tracking to telematics-derived engine run-hour and PTO-hour intervals to ensure accurate wear-cycle service.

### Example 3: Tier 2 Autonomous Operations (Human-in-the-Loop)
**User:** "Ground Bucket Truck #BK-412 immediately due to failed annual dielectric insulation testing and schedule shop servicing."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Bucket Truck #BK-412 has been placed into immediate Out-of-Service (OOS) status following a critical failure during annual dielectric insulation testing per ANSI/SIA A92.2 and OSHA 1910.269 standards.** **Telemetry and bench test records indicate elevated microampere leakage and compromised dielectric breakdown thresholds across the upper boom fiberglass insert and bucket liner.** **Immediate lockout/tagout (LOTO) protocols are initiated to prevent field deployment, and emergency priority bay scheduling is flagged for Central Fleet Maintenance.**

---

### Data Presentation

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Upper Boom Leakage Current (46 kV AC)** | 182.0 µA | ≤ 40.0 µA | +355.0% | **Critical** |
| **Lower Boom Insert Leakage (46 kV AC)** | 95.0 µA | ≤ 50.0 µA | +90.0% | **Critical** |
| **Bucket Liner Dielectric Integrity** | 140.0 µA (Pinhole Breach) | ≤ 50.0 µA | +180.0% | **Critical** |
| **Hydraulic Fluid Dielectric Breakdown** | 21.0 kV | ≥ 28.0 kV | -25.0% | **Warning** |
| **Asset Health Index (AHI)** | 28 / 100 | ≥ 85 / 100 | -67.1% | **Critical** |
| **Remaining Useful Life (RUL - Boom Assembly)** | 0.0 Operating Hours | N/A | -100.0% | **Critical** |

---

### Visualization Triggers
- **Recommended Visualization**: Grouped Bar Chart comparing measured leakage currents against standard ANSI/SIA A92.2 maximum allowable thresholds across boom components and bucket liners.


---

### Actionable Recommendations
- **Immediate LOTO Dispatch**: Apply physical Lockout/Tagout tags to the ignition and boom control console of `#BK-412` at the staging yard; quarantine vehicle keys in the Central Dispatch lockbox.
- **Shop Bay Routing**: Route `#BK-412` to Central Fleet Shop Bay 3 for detailed ultrasonic NDT (Non-Destructive Testing), boom interior cleaning/moisture bake-out, and bucket liner replacement.
- **Hydraulic Fluid Replacement**: Flush and replace non-conductive dielectric hydraulic fluid (ISO VG 15/22 dielectric oil) to restore breakdown strength above 30 kV.
- **Fleet Allocation Replacement**: Reassign Line Crew 12 to reserve unit `#BK-388` (certified compliant through Q3) to maintain scheduled distribution feeder maintenance.
- **Re-Certification Testing**: Mandate full-cycle high-potential (Hi-Pot) re-testing per ANSI/SIA A92.2-2021 prior to releasing the vehicle back to active duty.

---

### Executive Summary

While baseline contractual allowances are indexed to standard GSA/PUC emergency mobilization rates, multiple contractor invoices reflect unapproved surge pricing and unitemized incidental surcharges. Immediate clawback adjustments and exception reconciliation are required prior to final invoice settlement and FEMA/regulatory cost-recovery filing.**

### Actionable Recommendations
- **Invoice Line-Item Adjustments**: Issue formal billing dispute notices to visiting mutual aid contractors whose lodging and meal per diems exceed standard Regional Mutual Assistance Group (RMAG) schedule caps without pre-authorized emergency deviation waivers.
- **Enforce Fuel Card Indexing**: Mandate that fuel reconciliations adhere strictly to the localized OPIS (Oil Price Information Service) rack average plus contractually approved handling markups.
- **Receipt Reconciliation Mandate**: Require contractor administrative leads to submit itemized folio receipts for all lodging charges exceeding $185/night to verify whether hotel taxes/fees or unallowable ancillary charges caused the discrepancy.
- **Regulatory Cost-Recovery Documentation**: Archive all rate cap variance justifications and settlement audit trails to preserve eligibility for state public utility commission (PUC) prudency reviews and FEMA Category F/G public assistance reimbursements.

**User:** "Audit travel expense receipts, mileage logs, and daily per-diem submissions against FEMA disaster reimbursement guidelines."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary

Of the total $1,104,400 submitted across deployed responding utility crews, $999,600 meets all statutory substantiation standards, while $104,800 in claims has been flagged for audit variance or disallowance due to missing lodging itemization, unreceipted incidentals, and per-diem rate caps exceeding local GSA thresholds. Immediate adjustment and reconciliation are required prior to final Form FF-206-FY-21-137 submission to prevent federal clawbacks.**

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation

* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "What are the mandated Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) isolation points and PPE requirements for replacing a 13.8kV breaker in Cubicle 4?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Mandated Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) isolation for 13.8kV Cubicle 4 requires establishing a three-point electrical boundary encompassing upstream bus isolation, downstream load circuit opening, and auxiliary DC/AC control power disconnects. In accordance with NFPA 70E and OSHA 1910.269 standards, all personnel engaging in racking, testing, and grounding within the 13.8kV arc flash boundary must utilize minimum 40 cal/cm² (Arc Flash PPE Category 4) flash suits with Class 2 (17kV/20kV test) insulating rubber gloves. Physical work cannot commence until a calibrated Live-Dead-Live zero-energy verification is completed and protective safety grounds are secured.**

---

### Safety & Operational Boundaries: 13.8kV Switchgear Cubicle 4

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Voltage Rating** | 13.8 kV Line-to-Line | 13.8 kV Nominal | 0.0% | **Normal** |
| **Calculated Incident Energy** | 36.4 cal/cm² (@ 36 in) | < 40.0 cal/cm² (Cat 4 Limit) | -9.0% | **Warning** |
| **Arc Flash Boundary (AFB)** | 14.2 ft (170.4 in) | Standard Boundary Envelope | 0.0% | **Warning** |
| **Limited Approach Boundary** | 5.0 ft (60.0 in) | NFPA 70E Medium Voltage Std | 0.0% | **Normal** |
| **Restricted Approach Boundary**| 2.2 ft (26.0 in) | NFPA 70E Medium Voltage Std | 0.0% | **Critical** |
| **Control Circuit Voltage** | 125 VDC / 120 VAC | Nominal Trip/Close Supply | 0.0% | **Normal** |

---

### Mandated LOTO Isolation Sequence & Points

1. **Primary Circuit Isolation:**
   - **Primary Bus:** Trip and open 13.8kV circuit breaker in Cubicle 4.
   - **Racking Mechanism:** Rack out breaker from "Connected" to "Test" position, confirm visual separation/shutter closure, then move to "Disconnected/Fully Withdrawn" position.
   - **Upstream & Downstream Disconnects:** Open upstream bus tie/source disconnect switches and downstream feeder disconnects; attach LOTO padlocks and Danger Tags to physical mechanical locks.

2. **Secondary & Auxiliary Energy Isolation:**
   - **DC Control Power:** Open and lockout 125VDC breaker/knife switch in auxiliary control compartment to disable trip/close solenoids.
   - **AC Spring Charging:** Manually discharge breaker spring mechanism; open 120VAC motor supply circuit breaker and apply lockout hasp.
   - **PT/CT Circuits:** Isolate secondary potential transformer (PT) fuses to prevent backfeeding hazards; short-circuit secondary CT blocks prior to lead disconnection.

3. **Zero-Energy Verification (Live-Dead-Live):**
   - Perform three-point verification using an adequately rated capacitive voltage detector (rated ≥15kV):
     1. Test voltage detector against a known energized source/piezoelectric tester.
     2. Verify zero potential on all three phases ($A, B, C$) of Cubicle 4 primary stabs/bushings.
     3. Re-test voltage detector against the known source to verify proper instrument operation.
   - Install safety grounding cluster or racking ground truck to discharge residual capacitive charges.

---

### Mandated PPE Requirements (NFPA 70E / OSHA 1910.269)

* **Arc Flash Protective Equipment:** Minimum **40 cal/cm²** Arc Flash Hood with integrated face shield, multi-layer arc-rated jacket and bib overalls (or 40 cal/cm² flash suit).
* **Dielectric Protection:** ASTM D120 **Class 2 Rubber Insulating Gloves** (proof tested to 20kV AC, max use 17kV AC) with heavy-duty leather protectors.
* **Head, Eye & Hearing Protection:** Type I or II dielectric Hard Hat (Class E), safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), and canal earplugs/hearing protection.
* **Footwear & Apparel:** ASTM F2413 dielectric/EH-rated safety boots and non-melting arc-rated base layers (100% natural fiber/cotton).

---

### Visualization Triggers

```json
{
  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Cubicle 4 Incident Energy & Approach Boundaries (NFPA 70E)",
  "data": [
    {"parameter": "Restricted Approach", "distance_inches": 26, "type": "Approach Boundary"},
    {"parameter": "Limited Approach", "distance_inches": 60, "type": "Approach Boundary"},
    {"parameter": "Arc Flash Boundary", "distance_inches": 170.4, "type": "Arc Flash Envelope"},
    {"parameter": "Working Distance", "distance_inches": 36, "type": "Operating Point"}
  ]
}
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

* **Switching Order Issuance:** Request a formal Switching Order and Clearance Authorization from the System Operating Center (SOC) before initiating breaker manipulation.
* **Remote Racking Deployment:** Utilize a motorized remote racking mechanism positioned outside the 14.2 ft Arc Flash Boundary during breaker withdrawal and insertion.
* **Calibrated Test Equipment Check:** Ensure the high-voltage phased proximity detector is within its active calibration and recertification interval prior to Live-Dead-Live verification.
* **Safety Ground Placement:** Ensure grounds are sized to withstand maximum available short-circuit current (kA) for the required clearing time.

---

### [TIER 2 ACTION REQUIRED]

```json
  "action_type": "MEDIUM_VOLTAGE_PHYSICAL_ISOLATION",

  "isolation_points": [
    "Breaker 4 Racked to Disconnected Position",
    "125VDC Control Fuse Block Cubicle 4 Aux",
    "120VAC Spring Charging Disconnect SW-04",
    "Potential Transformer Secondary Disconnect Fuses"
  ],
  "ppe_mandate": "40 cal/cm2 Category 4 Suit + Class 2 Dielectric Gloves",
```

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary

### Site-Specific LOTO Switching Clearance Sheet: 115kV Transformer T-3

**Clearance ID:** CLR-115KV-T3-MAINT  
**Asset ID:** 115kV/13.8kV Substation Power Transformer T-3  
**Applicable Standards:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269, NFPA 70E (2024), IEEE 1584-2018  

#### Step-by-Step Switching & Isolation Sequence:
1. **Notification & Verification:** Notify System Operations Control Center (OCC) and Substation Switching Coordinator. Confirm no active auto-reclose or SCADA override conflicts.
2. **Trip & Open Low-Side Breaker:** Open and rack out 13.8kV Feeder Breaker 52-3L. Apply LOTO Lock & Red "DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE" Tag on the breaker cubicle mechanism.
3. **Open Low-Side Disconnect Switch:** Open Disconnect Switch 89-3L. Visually verify air-gap open on all 3 phases. Install lock and tag.
4. **Trip & Open High-Side Breaker:** Open 115kV Circuit Breaker 52-3H. Lock and tag control switch and open trip circuit isolators.
5. **Open High-Side Motor-Operated Disconnect (MOD):** Open 115kV Disconnect Switch 89-3H. Visually verify three-phase physical blade separation and mechanical lock in open position.
6. **Auxiliary & Control Isolation:** 
   - Open and lock DC control knife switches for T-3 LTC (Load Tap Changer) and sudden pressure relay trip circuits.
   - De-energize and LOTO 480V/240V AC cooling fan and oil pump auxiliary supply breaker panel (Panelboard AC-T3).
7. **Zero Energy Verification (Live-Dead-Live Test):**
   - Test voltage detector on known energized source.
   - Test 115kV bushings (H1, H2, H3) and 13.8kV bushings (X1, X2, X3) for zero voltage.
   - Retest voltage detector on known energized source to confirm detector functionality.
8. **Apply Protective Grounds:** Install approved portable personal protective grounds (minimum 4/0 AWG copper) to high-side 115kV and low-side 13.8kV terminals, ground-end connection attached first.

---

### PPE & Arc Flash Safety Checklist

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Arc Flash Rating** | $\ge 40\text{ cal/cm}^2$ (Category 4 Arc Flash Suit & Hood) | Racking breakers, opening manual disconnects, Live-Dead-Live testing |
| **Head & Face** | Hard hat with full-face arc shield, balaclava / arc flash hood | All switching & testing steps |
| **Eye & Ear** | ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection ($\ge 25\text{ NRR}$) | All clearance steps |
| **Hand Protection** | Class 4 (36kV rated) dielectric rubber gloves with leather protectors for 115kV; Class 2 for 13.8kV | Operating switches, voltage testing, ground installation |
| **Footwear** | EH-rated dielectric safety boots (ASTM F2413) | Substation yard maintenance |
| **Tools & Equipment** | Hot sticks rated for 115kV (tested per ASTM F711), calibrated phaser/detector | Zero-energy verification & ground placement |

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of employee fatigue risk monitor is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Employee Fatigue Risk Monitor Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank employee fatigue risk monitor events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation

* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_support_services.employee_fatigue_risk_monitor_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.

Lineworkers placed on designated standby receive a minimum daily standby stipend (typically 2.0 hours straight-time base pay per 24-hour cycle) until activated, after which emergency premium overtime rates apply. Call-outs enforce a mandatory minimum guarantee of 3.0 to 4.0 hours at premium pay (1.5x to 2.0x), accompanied by contractual meal stipends or hot meals provided at recurring 4-to-5-hour operational intervals.**

---

| **Mandatory Rest Period** | 8.0 consecutive hrs | 8.0 hrs Off-Duty | 0.0% | Normal |

### Detailed Contractual Breakdown

#### 1. Storm Standby (On-Call / Readiness)
* **Designation & Availability:** Linemen scheduled on pre-storm standby must remain fit for duty and within a 45-minute response radius to the reporting operating center.
* **Compensation:** Credited with **2.0 hours of straight-time base pay** per 24-hour standby period when not mobilized. 
* **Transition to Active Duty:** The moment an employee reports or is dispatched, standby pay terminates and active storm compensation shifts immediately to the applicable overtime multiplier (1.5x base hourly rate, escalating to 2.0x for Sundays, designated holidays, or hours exceeding 16 consecutive hours).

#### 2. Call-Out Minimums & Fatigue Rules
* **Guaranteed Minimum:** A minimum of **4.0 hours of compensation at the applicable overtime rate** applies to any emergency call-out outside regular shift hours, regardless of whether actual restoration takes less time.
* **Continuous Call-Out Window:** If a second call-out occurs within the original 4-hour window, it is considered part of the initial call-out block. Calls occurring after the initial window trigger a new call-out minimum.
* **16-Hour Rest Rule (Fatigue Management):** Linemen working 16 or more hours in a 24-hour period must receive a mandatory **8-hour uninterrupted rest period**. If this rest window extends into their regular scheduled shift, they receive regular straight-time pay for overlapping hours without performing field labor.

#### 3. Meal Allowances & Field Provisions
* **First Meal Eligibility:** Linemen called out on emergency storm duty become eligible for their first meal allowance after **2.0 hours of unplanned work** beyond regular shift hours, or at the start of an unscheduled call-out exceeding 4 hours.
* **Recurring Intervals:** Additional meal stipends ($22.50/meal) or employer-provided field catering must be provided every **4.5 to 5.0 hours** of sustained emergency work thereafter.
* **Paid Meal Time:** Lineworkers are allowed **30 minutes of paid meal time** when meals are taken in the field or at staging areas.

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of power purchase agreement legal reviewer is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Power Purchase Agreement Legal Reviewer Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank power purchase agreement legal reviewer events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_support_services.power_purchase_agreement_legal_reviewer_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "Does the commercial solar Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) include standard clauses for curtailment risk and negative pricing indemnity?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**A standard, commercially bankable commercial solar Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) must explicitly address economic and grid-directed curtailment as well as negative pricing risk allocation.** **Market-standard terms distinguish between Buyer-directed/Economic curtailment (which requires Deemed Generation compensation to the Seller) and System Emergency/RTO curtailment (which typically has an uncompensated annual cap before relief applies).** **Without affirmative negative pricing indemnity and economic curtailment compensation clauses, the project risks unhedged revenue erosion during negative wholesale LMP hours and high renewable penetration periods.**

---

### Contract Clause Review & Risk Matrix

| Metric / Clause Area | Current Standard Term | Baseline / Industry Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Economic Curtailment Settlement** | Compensated as Deemed Generation at Contract PPA Price | 100% Deemed Energy Compensation above Annual Cap | 0.0% | **Normal** |
| **Negative Pricing Floor Exposure** | Buyer absorbs negative LMP or pays floor price ($0/MWh) | Seller indemnified against negative settlement spread | 0.0% | **Normal** |
| **Emergency / RTO Curtailment Cap** | Uncompensated up to 50–100 hrs/yr (Buyer/RTO safe harbor) | Max 50 hrs/yr uncompensated threshold | +0.0% | **Warning** |
| **Environmental Attributes (RECs) on Curtailment** | Deemed REC value credit included in economic curtailment | 100% REC replacement/credit for Buyer-directed actions | 0.0% | **Normal** |
| **Interconnection / Force Majeure Curtailment** | Excused event without monetary compensation | Non-compensable, subject to COD/availability tolling | 0.0% | **Normal** |

---

### Detailed Legal & Commercial Analysis

#### 1. Curtailment Risk Allocation
* **Buyer-Directed / Economic Curtailment**: When the Buyer (or offtaker) orders the project to reduce or cease generation due to unfavorable wholesale market conditions, standard PPAs treat the foregone energy as **"Deemed Generation."** The Buyer pays the Seller the contract PPA rate for the estimated energy that would have been generated based on real-time solar irradiance telemetry minus actual delivered energy.
* **Emergency / ISO / RTO Curtailment**: Reductions ordered by the Regional Transmission Organization / Balancing Authority (e.g., CAISO, ERCOT, PJM) for grid stability or transmission congestion:
  * Standard clauses provide an **uncompensated annual allowance** (typically 50 to 100 equivalent full-capacity hours per contract year).
  * Any grid curtailment exceeding the agreed threshold is either treated as Deemed Generation or triggers contract availability relief to prevent Seller default under minimum generation guarantees.

#### 2. Negative Pricing Indemnity
* **Settlement Mechanism**: In wholesale nodal markets (Day-Ahead or Real-Time LMP), generation during negative price events incurs a settlement charge.
* **Standard Allocation**:
  * **Fixed-for-Floating / Virtual PPA**: The PPA price is fixed; if the nodal hub/bus settles below $0.00/MWh, the contract typically stipulates that the Buyer either indemnifies the Seller for negative nodal settlements, or the settlement calculation floors the market price at $0.00/MWh unless economic curtailment was ordered.
  * **Economic Turn-Down Protocol**: The PPA should define clear automated protocol instructions allowing the asset owner to automatically curtail inverter output when real-time LMP is below a contractually agreed negative threshold, preserving project economics.

---

### Actionable Recommendations

* **Audit Contractual Deemed Energy Formula**: Ensure the mathematical formulation for Deemed Generation utilizes calibrated on-site pyranometers/meteorological stations and the pre-agreed degradation curve rather than theoretical P50 estimates.
* **Define Specific Negative Pricing Thresholds**: Incorporate an express clause setting the negative LMP trigger point (e.g., `< -$0.00/MWh` or contract price differential) where automated inverter shutdown is authorized without violating availability guarantees.
* **Standardize RTO Curtailment Safe Harbors**: Limit uncompensated RTO/Reliability curtailment to no more than 50 hours per contract year to preserve project debt service coverage ratios (DSCR).
* **Legal Counsel Verification**: Submit revised contract schedules to outside energy regulatory counsel to confirm compliance with FERC Order 888 open-access rules and relevant RTO market tariff updates.

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis
**User:** "Analyze contractual availability guarantees, heat rate degradation terms, and environmental attribute transfer rules."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**A comprehensive legal and technical review of standard utility Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) provisions confirms that strict alignment between equivalent availability factors (EAF), thermal/efficiency heat rate degradation curves, and unencumbered title transfer of Environmental Attributes (RECs/GHG credits) is vital to risk mitigation. Non-conforming availability shortfall liquidated damages (LDs) and ambiguous heat rate test tolerances expose the off-taker to thermal dispatch cost shifting and market under-recovery. Contractual definitions must clearly establish WREGIS/NEPOOL-GIS/PJM-GATS tracking mechanisms alongside mandatory true-up settlement mechanisms to prevent double-counting and regulatory compliance exposure under FERC and state PUC mandates.**

---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Equivalent Availability Factor (EAF) Guarantee** | 94.20% | 96.50% | -2.38% | **Warning** |
| **Availability Shortfall LD Threshold** | $45.00/MWh-shortfall | Market Replace + $15/MWh | N/A | **Warning** |
| **Heat Rate Degradation Allowance (Annual)** | 1.15%/year | 0.85%/year | +35.29% | **Critical** |
| **Heat Rate Correction Testing Margin** | ±3.50% | ±1.50% (ASME PTC 46) | +133.33% | **Critical** |
| **Environmental Attribute Title Transfer Rate** | 100% Unbundled | 100% Bundled w/ Unit | 0.00% | **Normal** |
| **REC Delivery Failure Remedy (True-Up Penalty)** | Fixed $25.00/REC | Alternative Compliance Payment (ACP) Equivalent | -44.44% | **Critical** |
| **Force Majeure Outage Exclusion Window** | 180 Days Max | 90 Days Max | +100.00% | **Warning** |

---

### Key Contractual Review Dimensions

#### 1. Contractual Availability Guarantees & Liquidated Damages
* **Measurement Standard**: Governed by IEEE Standard 762 definitions for Equivalent Availability Factor (EAF) and Equivalent Forced Outage Rate (EFOR).
* **Planned Outage Windows**: Restrict major overhauls and planned outages to low-demand off-peak shoulder months (typically March–May, September–November) with a 60-day advance scheduling notice.
* **Liquidated Damages Mechanism**: Availability shortfalls below the guaranteed baseline must be calculated on an hourly replacement power cost basis ($\max(0, \text{Real-Time LMP} - \text{PPA Strike Price}) \times \text{Shortfall MWh}$) plus capacity deficiency penalties rather than fixed nominal rates.

#### 2. Heat Rate Degradation Terms & Efficiency Benchmarks
* **Degradation Profiles**: Ensure heat rate degradation schedules follow manufacturer warranty curves (e.g., OEM degradation curves) rather than linear over-approximations. Cumulative degradation caps must be enforced (e.g., maximum allowable heat rate increase not to exceed $4.5\%$ over a 20-year term).
* **Performance Testing Protocol**: Mandate annual heat rate performance verification conducted in accordance with ASME PTC 46 (Overall Plant Performance) under ISO standard ambient conditions (59°F, 14.7 psia, 60% relative humidity), disallowing excessive contractual deadbands.
* **Fuel Pass-Through Protection**: Where fuel costs are passed through to the off-taker, the heat rate used for settlement billing must be capped at the lesser of the actual tested heat rate or the contractually guaranteed degradation curve.

#### 3. Environmental Attribute Transfer Rules & Regulatory Title
* **Bundled Transfer Scope**: Legal definitions must grant the buyer 100% right, title, and interest in all current and future Environmental Attributes, including Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), carbon offsets, capacity rights, Clean Air Act Section 111 credits, and avoided GHG emissions associated with net generation.
* **Tracking System Conveyance**: Expressly obligate the seller to register, transfer, and deliver certificates through the designated regional tracking system (e.g., WREGIS, PJM-GATS, NEPOOL-GIS, ERCOT REC) by the 15th business day of the month following the generation month.
* **Warranty of Title & Indemnification**: Seller must provide explicit representations that all attributes are transferred free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, claims, or double-selling under competing compliance regimes (e.g., RPS, Clean Energy Standard, voluntary corporate claims).

---


---

### Actionable Recommendations

* **Amend Section 6.2 (Availability LDs)**: Redraft liquidated damage calculation formula from the static $45/MWh rate to an indexed market-replacement cost framework incorporating applicable RTO/ISO capacity deficiency charges.
* **Tighten Heat Rate Testing Clauses (Exhibit C)**: Re-index testing tolerances to ASME PTC 46 standards (±1.5%) and cap fuel pass-through settlements at the guaranteed degradation baseline.
* **Standardize REC Default Clauses (Section 11.4)**: Require replacement of defaulted RECs with equivalent vintage/eligibility attributes within 30 days, or apply an LD benchmarked to 120% of the prevailing state RPS Alternative Compliance Payment (ACP).
* **Limit Force Majeure Extended Relief**: Reduce the unilateral Force Majeure termination threshold from 180 consecutive days to 90 cumulative days per contract year to mitigate stranded capacity obligations.

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of dynamic real time pricing biller is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**

  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank dynamic real time pricing biller events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "How do five-minute wholesale LMP spot prices map to large industrial customer bills for yesterday's afternoon price spike?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Five-minute wholesale Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP) spot prices are mapped directly to large industrial accounts through interval meter telemetry adjusted for nodal marginal loss factors (MLF), ancillary service allocations, and capacity adders.** **During yesterday’s peak afternoon spike (14:30–16:30), wholesale nodal prices surged from \$42.50/MWh to a peak of \$2,100.00/MWh, driving the fully bundled dynamic Real-Time Pricing (RTP) rate to \$2,241.50/MWh.** **Industrial customers with automated demand response curtailed load by 54.6% during the top pricing intervals, successfully avoiding over \$142,800 in volumetric energy charges.**

---

### LMP-to-RTP Billing Transformation Architecture

To settle large industrial accounts on 5-minute dynamic pricing, the billing engine executes a multi-stage interval calculation:

1. **Telemetry & VEE Alignment**: 
   $$\text{Interval Energy } (E_t \text{ in MWh}) = \frac{\text{AMI Pulse/kW Accumulator}_t}{12}$$
   *Raw 5-minute interval kW telemetry passes through Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) prior to financial settlement.*

2. **Wholesale-to-Retail Bundled Rate Formulation**:
   $$\text{RTP Rate}_t (\$/\text{MWh}) = \Big( \text{LMP}_{\text{node}, t} \times (1 + \text{MLF}_{\text{feeder}}) \Big) + \text{Ancillary Adder}_t + \text{Capacity Adder}_t + \text{T\&D Delivery} + \text{Retail Admin Margin}$$
   * *Nodal LMP*: Five-minute Real-Time Settlement Point Price ($/MWh).
   * *Marginal Loss Factor (MLF)*: Dynamic or static expansion factor compensating for transmission/distribution losses (typically $1.035 - 1.065$).
   * *Ancillary & Reserve Adders*: Operating reserves (Spinning/Non-spinning) and Frequency Regulation charges allocated per interval.
   * *Delivery & Administrative Adders*: Fixed per-MWh distribution/transmission wheeling fees.

3. **Interval Financial Settlement**:
   $$\text{Total Dynamic Energy Charge} = \sum_{t=1}^{N} \Big( E_t \times \text{RTP Rate}_t \Big)$$

![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-billing%20and%20invoicing-blue)
![ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_ADK-v2.0-orange)
![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-Gemini_2.5_Pro-green)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of time of use charge calculator is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Time Of Use Charge Calculator Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank time of use charge calculator events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_billing_and_invoicing.time_of_use_charge_calculator_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "Are off-peak, mid-peak, and on-peak interval kWh accurately categorized for residential accounts under Tariff TOU-D?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**A comprehensive audit of residential AMI 15-minute interval data under Tariff TOU-D demonstrates an overall categorization accuracy of 99.48% across all billing cycles.** **Off-peak and mid-peak interval buckets remain fully compliant with tariff mapping definitions, while on-peak intervals exhibit minor boundary drift (0.32% misallocation) during Daylight Saving Time (DST) clock transitions.** **No systematic revenue leakage or cross-tier subsidy violations were detected, confirming that TOU-D billing calculations are robust and meet standard PUC regulatory compliance thresholds.**

---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Off-Peak Bucket Accuracy** | 99.85% | 99.50% | +0.35% | Normal |
| **Mid-Peak Bucket Accuracy** | 99.42% | 99.50% | -0.08% | Normal |
| **On-Peak Bucket Accuracy** | 99.18% | 99.50% | -0.32% | Warning |
| **VEE Validation Pass Rate** | 99.71% | 99.00% | +0.71% | Normal |
| **TOU Boundary Misallocation Leakage** | $412.50 | < $500.00 | -17.50% | Normal |
| **Aggregate TOU-D Billing Precision** | 99.48% | 99.50% | -0.02% | Normal |

---

### Visualization Triggers

A **Grouped Bar Chart** is recommended to monitor bucket-specific categorization compliance against the regulatory tariff baseline.

```json

  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Tariff TOU-D Interval Categorization Accuracy by Period",

  },

```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

- **Clock Synchronization Alignment**: Recalibrate head-end system (HES) to meter data management system (MDMS) time synchronization rules to resolve the 0.32% timestamp drift at the 16:00:00 on-peak boundary.
- **Targeted VEE Rule Refinement**: Deploy an automated Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) rule update in the billing engine specifically flagging interval readings spanning rate switch boundaries under Tariff TOU-D.
- **Exception Queue Processing**: Route the flagged misallocated intervals ($412.50 aggregate exposure) to the automated billing adjustment pipeline before the next billing statement finalization.

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis
**User:** "Evaluate the distribution of customer load shifting away from the 4 PM to 9 PM peak window since tariff migration."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Post-tariff migration analytics confirm an average peak demand reduction of 18.6% across residential and light commercial cohorts during the critical 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM on-peak window.** **The observed load shifting behavior has redistributed approximately 72.4% of curtailed on-peak volume into the super-off-peak (12:00 AM – 6:00 AM) and mid-day solar-soak (10:00 AM – 2:00 PM) rate bands, successfully flattening the system ramp rate.** **Overall net revenue impact remains revenue-neutral within target PUC rate-case bounds (+0.42% variance), while feeder-level peak loading constraints have decreased significantly across targeted distribution zones.**

---

---

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Residential (Default TOU-D-4-9PM)** | 420,500 | 3.48 | 2.85 | 1,324,575 kWh | Super Off-Peak (EV/Pre-Cooling) |
| **Residential w/ DER & Storage** | 68,200 | 2.95 | 1.12 | 624,030 kWh | Self-Consumption / Discharge |
| **Small Commercial (TOU-GS-1)** | 45,100 | 8.65 | 7.40 | 281,875 kWh | Mid-Day Solar Hours |
| **Medium Commercial (TOU-GS-2)** | 12,400 | 48.20 | 42.10 | 378,200 kWh | Morning Ramping (8 AM - 12 PM) |

---

```json
    }
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

1. **Target Non-Responding Cohorts with Behavioral Demand Response (BDR):**
   * Deploy localized automated energy insights and mid-peak alerts to the bottom 25th percentile of residential non-shifters located on capacity-constrained distribution feeders.

2. **Refine Solar Soak (Super-Off-Peak) Incentives:**
   * Evaluate expanding super-off-peak credit differentials between 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM in the upcoming rate design filing to absorb excess grid-edge solar generation and mitigate the late-afternoon duck-curve ramp.

3. **Continuous Revenue Leakage & Settlement Reconciliation:**
   * Maintain automated weekly VEE and shadow billing audits to ensure TOU multiplier billing determinates match wholesale CAISO/regional market settlements with zero unbilled interval leakage.

### Example 3: Tier 2 Autonomous Operations (Human-in-the-Loop)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of dark spread heat rate calculator is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Dark Spread Heat Rate Calculator Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank dark spread heat rate calculator events for immediate action.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation

* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "What is the current dark spread ($/MWh) for our 600 MW supercritical coal plant given wholesale power and delivered coal costs?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**The gross dark spread for the 600 MW supercritical coal generating unit currently stands at $26.94/MWh based on an on-peak wholesale power LMP of $48.50/MWh and a delivered fuel cost of $21.56/MWh (8.80 MMBtu/MWh heat rate @ $2.45/MMBtu). Factoring in regional carbon allowance pricing ($10.00/ton @ 0.88 ton/MWh emission intensity) and Variable O&M ($4.50/MWh), the Net Clean Dark Spread is $13.64/MWh, maintaining positive operating margin across all standard on-peak hours.**

---

### Quantitative Performance Metrics

$$\text{Gross Dark Spread } (\$/\text{MWh}) = \text{Power LMP} - (\text{Delivered Coal Price } [\$/\text{MMBtu}] \times \text{Heat Rate } [\text{MMBtu/MWh}])$$

$$\text{Clean Dark Spread } (\$/\text{MWh}) = \text{Gross Dark Spread} - (\text{Carbon Price} \times \text{CO}_2 \text{ Emission Factor}) - \text{VOM}$$

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wholesale Day-Ahead LMP (On-Peak)** | $48.50/MWh | $45.00/MWh | +7.78% | Normal |
| **Delivered Coal Cost** | $2.45/MMBtu | $2.30/MMBtu | +6.52% | Normal |
| **Supercritical Net Heat Rate** | 8.80 MMBtu/MWh | 8.75 MMBtu/MWh | +0.57% | Normal |
| **Fuel Component Cost** | $21.56/MWh | $20.13/MWh | +7.10% | Normal |
| **Gross Dark Spread** | **$26.94/MWh** | **$24.87/MWh** | **+8.32%** | Normal |
| **Variable O&M (VOM)** | $4.50/MWh | $4.20/MWh | +7.14% | Normal |
| **$\text{CO}_2$ Compliance Cost** (0.88 t/MWh @ $10/t) | $8.80/MWh | $8.00/MWh | +10.00% | Warning |
| **Net Clean Dark Spread (CDS)** | **$13.64/MWh** | **$12.67/MWh** | **+7.66%** | Normal |
| **Unit Output (Economic Dispatch)** | 540 MW (90% Cap) | 480 MW (80% Cap) | +12.50% | Normal |

---

### Visualization: Dark Spread Dispatch Breakdown

```json
    },

    }

}
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

- **Dispatch Bidding Optimization**: Submit Day-Ahead physical offers targeting full economic maximum (600 MW) during the HE 07:00–22:00 on-peak window where the Net CDS exceeds the $10.00/MWh hurdle threshold.
- **Off-Peak Cycling Assessment**: With off-peak Net Clean Dark Spread at -$0.36/MWh, evaluate reducing generation to the plant's minimum stable load (Pmin: 240 MW) rather than taking unit offline to avoid startup/shutdown thermal stress cycles.
- **Fuel & Allowance Hedging**: Execute forward coal purchase contracts for Q3/Q4 if rail transportation surcharges rise, locking in spark/dark spread hedges on Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) for expected baseload generation tranches.

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis
**User:** "Evaluate plant operational heat rates (Btu/kWh) across partial loading points to determine minimum profitable generation thresholds."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Thermal efficiency deteriorates significantly at low operating points, where unit heat rates increase from a baseline of 9,050 Btu/kWh at 100% Maximum Continuous Rating (MCR) to 12,450 Btu/kWh at 25% minimum stable generation ($P_{min}$), a +37.57% heat rate penalty.** **To maintain a positive Clean Dark Spread under benchmark delivered coal pricing ($2.75/MMBtu) and variable environmental/O&M costs ($7.75/MWh), the minimum profitable Locational Marginal Price (LMP) threshold escalates from $32.64/MWh at full output to $41.99/MWh at $P_{min}$.** **Operating below 40% loading (240 MW) exposes the asset to negative operating margins if clearing LMPs fall below $37.59/MWh, requiring multi-part bid curve segmentation to ensure startup, no-load, and incremental energy costs are fully recovered.**

---

### Quantitative Evaluation: Heat Rate & Generation Thresholds

The table below details thermal efficiency, short-run marginal cost (SRMC), and break-even generation thresholds across discrete plant loading increments for a reference 600 MW subcritical/supercritical coal unit:

$$\text{SRMC } (\$/\text{MWh}) = \left(\text{Heat Rate } \left[\frac{\text{Btu}}{\text{kWh}}\right] \times 10^{-3} \times \text{Delivered Coal Price } \left[\frac{\$}{\text{MMBtu}}\right]\right) + \text{VOM} + \text{Emission Costs}$$

$$\text{Clean Dark Spread (CDS) } (\$/\text{MWh}) = \text{LMP} - \text{SRMC}$$

*Parameters: Delivered Coal Price = $2.75/MMBtu; Variable O&M (VOM) = $4.50/MWh; Emissions Allowance Cost ($\text{SO}_2, \text{NO}_x, \text{CO}_2$) = $3.25/MWh; Market LMP Reference = $42.50/MWh.*

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **100% Load (600 MW) Heat Rate** | 9,050 Btu/kWh | 9,050 Btu/kWh | 0.00% | Normal |
| **100% Load Break-Even LMP** | $32.64 / MWh | $32.64 / MWh | 0.00% | Normal |
| **100% Load Clean Dark Spread** | +$9.86 / MWh | +$10.00 / MWh | -1.40% | Normal |
| **80% Load (480 MW) Heat Rate** | 9,350 Btu/kWh | 9,050 Btu/kWh | +3.31% | Normal |
| **80% Load Break-Even LMP** | $33.46 / MWh | $32.64 / MWh | +2.51% | Normal |
| **60% Load (360 MW) Heat Rate** | 9,850 Btu/kWh | 9,050 Btu/kWh | +8.84% | Normal |
| **60% Load Break-Even LMP** | $34.84 / MWh | $32.64 / MWh | +6.74% | Normal |
| **40% Load (240 MW) Heat Rate** | 10,850 Btu/kWh | 9,050 Btu/kWh | +19.89% | Warning |
| **40% Load Break-Even LMP** | $37.59 / MWh | $32.64 / MWh | +15.17% | Warning |
| **25% Load ($P_{min}$ 150 MW) Heat Rate** | 12,450 Btu/kWh | 9,050 Btu/kWh | +37.57% | Critical |
| **25% Load Break-Even LMP** | $41.99 / MWh | $32.64 / MWh | +28.65% | Critical |
| **25% Load Clean Dark Spread** | +$0.51 / MWh | +$10.00 / MWh | -94.90% | Critical |

---

### Actionable Recommendations

1. **Segmented Multi-Part Offer Curves**:
   - Construct Day-Ahead and Real-Time offer curves with monotonically increasing piecewise segments reflecting the incremental heat rate (IHR), rather than an average unit heat rate.
   - Price Block 1 (0 to 150 MW, $P_{min}$) at **$41.99/MWh** minimum to prevent unrecovered fixed/no-load fuel penalties.
   - Price Incremental Blocks (150–360 MW, 360–480 MW, 480–600 MW) at **$30.55/MWh**, **$30.93/MWh**, and **$30.82/MWh** incremental SRMC respectively.

2. **Economic Turndown vs. Cycling Evaluation**:
   - When off-peak LMPs fall between **$33.00/MWh and $41.00/MWh**, maintain unit online at $P_{min}$ only if expected day-ahead restart/shutdown cycle costs (boiler stress, startup fuel, aux power) exceed the intra-day Clean Dark Spread operating deficit.
   - For sustained multi-day pricing forecasts $< \$37.00/\text{MWh}$, transition asset status to economic decommit.

3. **Fuel & Heat Rate Telemetry Integration**:
   - Continuously update boiler efficiency coefficients from plant distributed control systems (DCS) using as-burned coal calorific value (HHV/LHV) and ambient condenser backpressure data to avoid miscalculated dark spreads during ambient temperature swings.

### Example 3: Tier 2 Autonomous Operations (Human-in-the-Loop)

In accordance with utility safety and market governance protocols, autonomous submission of generation commitment schedules to the Independent System Operator (ISO) constitutes a Tier 2 physical/financial market action. A finalized commitment schedule has been calculated and staged for mandatory Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval prior to ISO market clearing submission.**

### Executive Summary
**Thermal overloads on critical transmission corridors force Real-Time Dispatch (RTD) optimization engines to exhaust fast-ramping localized units, triggering ramp-rate constraints that decouple nodal marginal costs from system-wide energy pricing.** **When ramping shortages cause temporary infeasibilities or unphysical shadow price spikes in the ex-ante RTD run, ISO/RTO market monitors enact ex-post price corrections to recalculate LMPs based on relaxed transmission penalties or verified physical unit capability.** **This structural divergence creates settlement variance between physical telemetry, five-minute dispatch instructions, and final settled nodal prices.**

---

### Mechanics of Correlation

```
Transmission Thermal Overload (>100% MVA Rating)
   │
   ▼
Localized Counter-Flow Dispatch Required
   │
   ▼
Generator Ramp Rate Saturation (MW/min Limit Hit)
   │
   ▼
RTD Infeasibility / Scarcity Penalty Shadow Pricing ($1,000–$2,000/MWh)
   │
   ▼
Ex-Post Tariff Screening / Price Correction (Relaxation to Physical Incremental Cost)
```

1. **Thermal Line Overload & Shadow Price Dynamics**: As power flows exceed the Normal/Emergency MVA ratings of a transmission element, the Security Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED/RTD) algorithm applies a Lagrange multiplier ($\lambda_{flow}$) to re-dispatch generation. If local effective generation is limited, the congestion component ($LMP_{cong}$) escalates non-linearly.
2. **Ramp-Rate Binding**: Fast-ramping generation becomes constrained by physical ramp limits ($\Delta MW / \Delta t$). When the marginal unit cannot ramp fast enough to relieve the transmission constraint within the 5-minute dispatch interval, the optimization hits a mathematical constraint infeasibility, imposing an administrative power balance or transmission penalty factor.
3. **Ex-Post Price Correction**: ISO/RTO market software recalculates settlement LMPs post-interval if the price spike was driven by mathematical infeasibility, transient software anomalies, or modeling artifacts rather than a true physical capacity deficit. The ex-post run recalculates LMPs with constraint relaxation parameters, resulting in substantial downward price adjustments relative to real-time ex-ante indications.

# ⚡ Natural Gas Pipeline Constraint Analyzer

![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-wholesale%20trading-blue)
![ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_ADK-v2.0-orange)
![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-Gemini_2.5_Pro-green)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of natural gas pipeline constraint analyzer is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Natural Gas Pipeline Constraint Analyzer Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank natural gas pipeline constraint analyzer events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_wholesale_trading.natural_gas_pipeline_constraint_analyzer_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "Are there any Critical Notices or Operational Flow Orders (OFO) declared on major interstate natural gas pipelines feeding our plants?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**A critical Operational Flow Order (OFO) Type 6 (Under-Performance / Short Imbalance) has been issued on Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco) Zone 5/6 and Algonquin Gas Transmission due to severe cold weather-driven demand spikes and compressor station constraints. Additionally, Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) M3 has issued a Critical Notice restricting secondary firm and interruptible transportation (IT) services. All gas-fired generation units interconnected to these paths face strict non-compliance balancing penalties ($25.00/MMBtu + index) and must balance intraday burn within a tight ±3% tolerance band.**

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis
**User:** "Analyze how ambient intake air temperature impacts gas turbine heat rate efficiency and power output degradation."

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Ambient intake air temperature has an inverse relationship with gas turbine capacity and a direct degrading impact on heat rate efficiency due to air density variation.** **For standard heavy-duty combustion turbines (e.g., F- and H-Class frames), every 10°F increase in ambient temperature above ISO base conditions (59°F / 15°C) yields an estimated 3.0% to 4.5% reduction in net power output and a 1.2% to 1.8% increase (degradation) in net heat rate (Btu/kWh).** **In wholesale energy markets, this thermodynamic derate simultaneously compresses generation capacity and increases variable fuel cost, requiring dynamic adjustment of unit dispatch bids and Clean/Dark Spark Spread calculations during extreme summer peak intervals.**

---

### Thermodynamic Principles & Degradation Mechanisms

1. **Air Density & Mass Flow Rate**: Gas turbines are constant volumetric flow machines. The mass flow rate ($\dot{m} = \rho \cdot \dot{V}$) entering the axial compressor is directly proportional to intake air density ($\rho = \frac{P_{amb}}{R \cdot T_{amb}}$). Elevated ambient temperatures lower air density, reducing mass flow and limiting total expansion mass across the turbine blades.
2. **Compressor Specific Work**: Warmer intake air increases the specific compression work required per unit mass ($W_c = c_p \cdot T_1 [r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma} - 1]$), consuming a higher fraction of gross turbine output.
3. **Turbine Firing Temperature & Exhaust Backpressure Limits**: Higher compressor discharge temperatures ($T_2$) restrict maximum fuel firing limits to maintain hot gas path component metallurgical integrity, worsening net thermal efficiency.

---

### Performance Sensitivity Matrix (Relative to ISO Baseline: 59°F / 15°C, 60% RH, 14.696 psia)

| Metric | Current Value (Peak Summer 105°F) | Baseline / Target (ISO 59°F) | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |

| **Combustion Turbine Net Output** | 191.1 MW | 230.0 MW | -16.9% | Critical |
| **Net Heat Rate (LHV)** | 7,690 Btu/kWh | 7,050 Btu/kWh | +9.08% (Degraded) | Critical |
| **Air Mass Flow Rate** | 1,048 lb/s | 1,225 lb/s | -14.4% | Critical |
| **Compressor Power Consumption** | 134.5 MW | 126.2 MW | +6.58% | Warning |
| **Gross Thermal Efficiency (LHV)** | 44.37% | 48.40% | -8.33% | Warning |
| **Fuel Burn per MWh Generation** | 7.69 MMBtu/MWh | 7.05 MMBtu/MWh | +9.08% | Critical |

*Table: Standard representative performance impact for a 230 MW F-Class simple-cycle combustion turbine across ambient extremes.*

---

### Wholesale Trading & Spark Spread Margin Impact

The thermodynamic heat rate derate translates directly into financial exposure within real-time and day-ahead LMP markets via the **Spark Spread formula**:

$$\text{Spark Spread } (\$/\text{MWh}) = P_{\text{power}} - (\text{Heat Rate} \times P_{\text{gas}}) - \text{VOM}$$

- **Marginal Fuel Cost Shift**: At a natural gas hub price of \$3.50/MMBtu, an increase in heat rate from 7,050 to 7,690 Btu/kWh increases the unit's marginal fuel cost by **\$2.24/MWh** (\$24.68 vs. \$26.92/MWh).
- **Available Margin Compression**: Failure to update supply curves with ambient-adjusted heat rate curves risks dispatching the asset below its actual marginal cost during real-time heat waves.

# ⚡ Portfolio Value At Risk Analyzer

![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-wholesale%20trading-blue)
![ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_ADK-v2.0-orange)
![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-Gemini_2.5_Pro-green)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of portfolio value at risk analyzer is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Portfolio Value At Risk Analyzer Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank portfolio value at risk analyzer events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_wholesale_trading.portfolio_value_at_risk_analyzer_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "What is our wholesale energy portfolio 99% one-day Value at Risk (VaR) under a simulated 20% natural gas price spike?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Under a simulated +20% natural gas commodity price spike (from $2.75/MMBtu to $3.30/MMBtu), the wholesale energy portfolio’s 1-day 99% Value at Risk (VaR) increases from the baseline of $4.20M to $8.65M (+105.95%). The primary risk driver is the portfolio's unhedged short power exposure and variable heat rate spark-spread erosion across uncommitted gas peakers and open spot obligations. Total downside risk breaches the enterprise operational tolerance threshold ($7.50M), transitioning the risk profile to a Warning/Critical threshold.**

---

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of ancillary services bid optimizer is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers

  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank ancillary services bid optimizer events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation

* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_wholesale_trading.ancillary_services_bid_optimizer_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "How should we allocate our 100 MW flexible gas turbine capacity between Regulation Up, Spinning Reserve, and Day-Ahead Energy?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Optimal allocation of the 100 MW flexible gas turbine between Day-Ahead (DA) Energy, Regulation Up (Reg-Up), and Spinning Reserve requires a dynamic co-optimization model driven by the spread between Locational Marginal Prices (LMP) and Ancillary Service Market Clearing Prices (MCP). Because flexible gas turbines possess high ramp rates ($>10\text{ MW/min}$) and fast start capabilities, maximizing margin requires allocating upper capacity headroom to high-value Reg-Up and Spinning Reserve during tight regulation hours, while committing base capacity to DA Energy when spark spreads exceed ancillary opportunity costs. Operating at $P_{min}$ (e.g., 40 MW) base energy with 30 MW Reg-Up and 30 MW Spinning Reserve yields the highest risk-adjusted net margin during volatile grid intervals.**

---

### 1. Capacity Allocation Framework & Physical Constraints

To co-optimize the 100 MW asset without violating physical operating parameters or NERC/ISO market rules:

$$\max \Pi = (LMP - \text{Marginal Cost}) \cdot P_{\text{DA}} + MCP_{\text{RegUp}} \cdot C_{\text{RegUp}} + MCP_{\text{Spin}} \cdot C_{\text{Spin}} - \text{Mileage Degradation Cost}$$

$$\text{Subject to:}$$
$$P_{\text{DA}} + C_{\text{RegUp}} + C_{\text{Spin}} \le 100\text{ MW } (P_{\max})$$
$$P_{\text{DA}} - C_{\text{RegDown}} \ge P_{\min} \quad (\approx 40\text{ MW if online})$$
$$C_{\text{RegUp}} \le \text{Ramp Rate} \times 5\text{ min} \quad (\le 50\text{ MW at } 10\text{ MW/min})$$
$$C_{\text{Spin}} \le \text{Ramp Rate} \times 10\text{ min} \quad (\le 100\text{ MW at } 10\text{ MW/min})$$

---

### 2. Market Metric Benchmarks & Optimization Performance

| **Reg-Up / DA Energy Price Ratio** | 1.38 | 0.85 | +62.4% | **Warning** |

| **Heat Rate Degradation Penalty** | $185.00/hr | $150.00/hr | +23.3% | **Normal** |

---

### 3. Recommended Allocation Matrix by Market Regime

1. **High Renewable Ramp / Morning & Evening Duck Curve (Recommended Base Case)**:
   * **DA Energy Commitment**: 40 MW (Set at $P_{\min}$ to maintain online status).
   * **Regulation Up Bid**: 30 MW (Captures elevated 5-minute regulation mileage clearing prices).
   * **Spinning Reserve Bid**: 30 MW (Synchronized headroom monetized with zero incremental fuel burn).
   * *Net Headroom Utilization*: 100% (40 MW Energy + 30 MW RegUp + 30 MW Spin = 100 MW).

2. **Scarcity / High LMP Events ($LMP > \text{Heat Rate} \times \text{Fuel} + \$80/\text{MWh}$)**:
   * **DA Energy Commitment**: 75 MW.
   * **Regulation Up Bid**: 0 MW (Avoid de-rating base generation during price spikes).
   * **Spinning Reserve Bid**: 25 MW (Top 25 MW headroom delivered as contingency spin).

3. **Low LMP / High Regulation Value Regimes ($MCP_{\text{RegUp}} > LMP - \text{MC}$)**:
   * **DA Energy Commitment**: 40 MW ($P_{\min}$).
   * **Regulation Up Bid**: 50 MW (Ramp-limited maximum 5-minute capacity).
   * **Spinning Reserve Bid**: 10 MW.

# ⚡ Reactive Power Capacitor Dispatcher

![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-grid%20balancing-blue)
![ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_ADK-v2.0-orange)
![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-Gemini_2.5_Pro-green)

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of reactive power capacitor dispatcher is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — Reactive Power Capacitor Dispatcher Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank reactive power capacitor dispatcher events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_grid_balancing.reactive_power_capacitor_dispatcher_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "Which distribution substations are currently exhibiting a lagging power factor below 0.92 during heavy inductive motor loading?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Real-time telemetry analysis identifies four distribution substations operating below the utility target power factor threshold of 0.95 lagging, specifically falling below 0.92 lagging under heavy industrial and pumping inductive motor load profiles. Substation `SUB-402 (Oakridge Industrial)` exhibits the most severe deficit at 0.86 lagging with a 14.8 MVAR uncompensated reactive power demand. Immediate multi-stage shunt capacitor bank dispatch is required to normalize bus voltages, mitigate line losses, and restore compliance with IEEE 519 / NERC standard operational criteria.**

---

### Data Presentation

| **SUB-118 (Pine Valley Mfg) PF** | 0.88 Lagging | 0.95 Lagging | -7.37% | **Critical** |
| **SUB-305 (Harbor Pumping) PF** | 0.89 Lagging | 0.95 Lagging | -6.32% | **Warning** |
| **SUB-221 (North Commercial) PF** | 0.91 Lagging | 0.95 Lagging | -4.21% | **Warning** |
| **Total System Reactive Deficit** | 38.4 MVAR | 0.0 MVAR Target | +100.0% | **Critical** |
| **Average Substation Bus Voltage** | 0.962 p.u. | 1.000 p.u. | -3.80% | **Warning** |

#### 2. Substation Telemetry & Reactive Loading Breakdown
| Substation ID | Feeder ID | Active Power (MW) | Reactive Power (MVAR) | Power Factor | Inductive Load Type | Required MVAR Compensation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SUB-402** | FDR-402-A/B | 25.2 MW | 14.8 MVAR | **0.86 Lagging** | Heavy Industrial Induction Motors | +9.6 MVAR |
| **SUB-118** | FDR-118-C | 18.5 MW | 9.9 MVAR | **0.88 Lagging** | Manufacturing / Extrusion Drives | +5.8 MVAR |
| **SUB-305** | FDR-305-1 | 14.0 MW | 7.2 MVAR | **0.89 Lagging** | Municipal Water Pumping Arrays | +4.1 MVAR |
| **SUB-221** | FDR-221-E | 21.0 MW | 9.6 MVAR | **0.91 Lagging** | Large HVAC Chiller Compressors | +3.5 MVAR |

---

### Visualization Trigger

- **Engage Downstream Distribution Feeder Switched Banks**: Issue close commands to automated pole-mounted switched capacitor banks on `FDR-305-1` and `FDR-221-E` to support mid-feeder voltage profiles.
- **Monitor Tap Changer Interactions**: Verify that Load Tap Changers (LTC) and Voltage Regulators do not experience excessive tap hunting during reactive step insertion.
- **Coordination Alert**: Notify the Industrial Account Management representative if continuous uncompensated motor operation at `SUB-402` breaches contractual power factor penalty tariffs (< 0.90 lagging).

(+3.90%). Feeder-head power factor improves from 0.865 lagging to 0.982 lagging, significantly reducing upstream reactive power demand and lowering circuit technical $I^2R$ line losses by 18.4%. This dispatch action successfully brings all feeder nodes within ANSI C84.1 Range A voltage requirements (0.950 – 1.050 p.u.).**

# ⚡ System Inertia Tracker

## 🏢 Business Problem
In the fast-paced and highly regulated Energy & Utilities sector, manual tracking and analysis of system inertia tracker is inherently error-prone, fragmented, and slow. Unresolved inefficiencies in this area quietly erode capital efficiency, impact grid reliability, and increase the risk of regulatory penalties or catastrophic outages. This autonomous agent continuously audits telemetry, financial data, and maintenance logs, applying advanced analytical rules to identify active anomalies and critical faults early. By autonomously flagging these risks, the agent protects infrastructure reliability, optimizes workforce deployment, and defers millions in CapEx and OpEx.

## 🎯 What It Answers
* **Routed to Data Insights (BigQuery):**
  * **Capability 1** — System Inertia Tracker Anomaly Detection: flags statistical outliers, match confidence scores, and historical degradation curves.
  * **Capability 2** — Operational Prioritization: cross-references load history and risk models to rank system inertia tracker events for immediate action.
* **Routed to External Grounding / Simulation:**
  * **Capability 3** — Industry Benchmarking: retrieves standard IEEE/FERC compliance rules and benchmarks based on current operating metrics.

## ⚙️ Architecture & ADK Implementation
* **Task Lead:** `agent.py` coordinates the A2A workflow.
* **Worker Agent:** Queries the `utilities_grid_balancing.system_inertia_tracker_logs` BigQuery table using the `BigQueryQueryTool` governed by `business_rules.md`.
* **Critic Agent:** Enforces structural formatting and scrubs PII based on `safety_guardrails.md`.

## 💬 Agent Response Examples

### Example 1: Operational Diagnostic Query
**User:** "What is the real-time synchronous grid inertia level in megawatt-seconds across the interconnect, and does it exceed NERC safety floors?"

**Agent Response:**
### Executive Summary
**Real-time synchronous grid inertia across the Interconnect is currently operating at 151,200 MW·s, which remains 16.31% above the NERC Minimum Safety Floor of 130,000 MW·s and well above the Critical Floor threshold of 100,000 MW·s.** **While current inertia levels comply with mandatory NERC BAL-003 frequency response and reliability standards, a negative rate of change (-10.27% over the past 60 minutes) has been detected due to midday thermal de-commitments and high inverter-based resource (IBR) penetration.** **System stability margins remain adequate, but proactive monitoring of the Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) is warranted as peak solar displacement continues.**

---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Synchronous Inertia ($H_{sys}$)** | 151,200 MW·s | 175,000 MW·s (Nominal Target) | -13.60% | **Normal** |
| **NERC Minimum Safety Floor** | 151,200 MW·s | 130,000 MW·s (NERC Threshold) | +16.31% | **Normal** |
| **NERC Critical Floor Limit** | 151,200 MW·s | 100,000 MW·s (Critical Min) | +51.20% | **Normal** |
| **Estimated System RoCoF (N-1 Loss of 2.7 GW)** | 0.178 Hz/s | < 0.250 Hz/s (Reliability Limit) | -28.80% | **Normal** |
| **Synchronous Kinetic Energy Ratio** | 68.4% | > 60.0% (Operational Rule) | +14.00% | **Normal** |

* **Fast Frequency Response (FFR) Readiness**: Verify that Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and synthetic inertia resources with droop settings $\le 3\%$ are armed for sub-second primary frequency response in case of a largest single contingency (N-1) trip.

### Example 2: Trend & Comparative Analysis

### Executive Summary
**Yes, the industrial park on Feeder 8 experienced an ITIC (Information Technology Industry Council) curve-violating voltage sag during the transmission fault at 03:14:22 UTC.** The line-to-ground fault caused the RMS voltage at Feeder 8 substation bus to drop to **0.68 pu (68% of nominal)** for a duration of **140 ms (8.4 cycles)** before clearing. Because the retained voltage fell below the 0.70 pu ITIC lower tolerance boundary for durations between 20 ms and 500 ms, the event entered the "No Damage / Tripping Likely" prohibited region.

---

### Data Presentation
